figures.caption: Figure 1: Shows conditions that may arise using cosine similarity as s(·, ·) and random anchors and their effect on RR: i) The dimensionality collapse of linearly dependent anchors. ii) How s(·, ·) amplifies noise in anchors close to (0, 0). iii) s(·, ·) invariance to certain affine transformations.

Figure 2: Effect of s(·, ·) on RR geometry under cross-space distortions. Left: original clustered space and two deformed versions (rotation + scaling + translation). Right: RR coordinates computed with different similarities and the cosine similarity between the resulting RR spaces.

Table 1: Stitching performance with CNN- and Transformer-based encoders on CIFAR-100 (coarse). Mean-weighted F1 (± std) across 6 seeds with m=300 anchors. Rows indicate the test encoder (where evaluation happens). The classifier column indicates the encoder whose RR features the classifier was trained on. The classifiers are RexNet-100, ViT-small-patch16-224, ViT-base-patch16-224, ViT-base-resnet50-384.
Table 2: Stitching performance with different language-based encoders. The table shows the mean-weighted F1 (± std) across 6 seeds. Run with 300 anchors.
Table 3: Stitching performance with small language models between a Source and Zero-shot encoder. Shows retrieval at one (R@1) and five (R@5) on the generated dataset across different seeds.
Figure 3: Ablation across anchor counts for anchor construction (random vs. PARAM) and similarity (cosine vs. WIP).

Figure 4: Effect of support-set size (|Xsub|) on CIFAR-100 zero-shot performance. After roughly 5,000–10,000 parallel points (≈10–20% of the dataset), gains diminish substantially, with performance saturating as more points are added.
Table 5: Hyperparameters used for PARAM–WIP training and evaluation.
Table 6: Extension of the results from Section 6. The table shows the mean-weighted F1 (± std) across 6 seeds. Run with 300 anchors.

Table 7: Extension of the results from Section 6. Shows stitching performance with small language models. Mean retrieval accuracy (%) (± std) across seeds. Shows retrieval at one (R@1) and five (R@5) accuracy on the generated dataset.

Figure 5: MNIST reconstruction with an anisotropic latent space. The bottom 2 rows are zero-shot stitching using RR. The PCA plot (right) illustrates the induced "cigar-shaped" latent distribution. Latent space dim and number of anchors are set to 64.
